s1.syndrome_frame: Enlarging, painful, purplish mass in the ear canal with granulomatous inflammation and atypical cells
salient_findings: Purplish-red mass in the left external ear canal
Irregular, friable surface with bleeding on minimal contact
Lobulated mass extending into the external acoustic canal and parotid space
Bilateral cervical lymph nodes up to 0.6 cm in diameter
Marked vascularity of the mass
key_facts: Purplish lump in the left ear canal
Cracking and pus-filled sores at the site
Contrast-enhanced CT showed a lobulated mass
Incisional biopsy revealed atypical cells and granulomatous inflammation

shortlist.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive tumor with rapid growth, pain, and bleeding, consistent with clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and atypical cells on biopsy, matching the syndrome frame

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Highly vascular tumor with rapid growth, consistent with CT angiography findings

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cervical lymph node involvement and atypical cells on biopsy, suggesting a possible lymphoid malignancy

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Marked vascularity on CT angiography and bleeding on minimal contact, consistent with a highly vascular tumor

raw.rationale: The presence of a rapidly enlarging, painful, and bleeding mass in a child, along with atypical cells on biopsy, is most consistent with Rhabdomyosarcoma, a common soft tissue sarcoma in children.

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with multiple lesions and systemic symptoms, not a single enlarging mass

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: More commonly affects bones and has distinct histological features not mentioned in the biopsy results

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Would not typically present as a single, painful, and bleeding mass in the ear canal

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: Rare in children and usually presents with more pronounced vascular features and distinct histology
